## PDF page 236

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=236)

```text
                    SHOVING PREFLOP


Now the spot is reversed and you will calculate the EV when you are the one
going all-in preflop. This requires that you use the advanced EV formula since
there are three branches to consider:

   ●   You go all-in and your opponent folds

   ●   You go all-in, get called, and you win the pot

   ●   You go all-in, get called, and you lose the pot

These culminating exercises will tie together many concepts from this
workbook and force you to sink or swim. Take your time with them and feel
free to revisit the Moderate EV and Advanced EV chapters if need be.

Each page contains a single all-in scenario. Start by reading the prompt and
discerning the key information. On the right is the range you assume your
opponent has after their last action.

Begin with the first range that they might call your all-in with.

To figure out how often they will fold to your all-in, remember to do 100%-
(their continuance range/their original range). If the range on the right is 15%
and their continuance range is 5%, then they are folding 2/3 of the time.

PRO TIP: when considering preflop ranges and blockers, it can help to work in
combo form. And 100%-(continuance combos/original combos) is equivalent.

                                    PA G E 2 3 6
```

begin filling out the EV formula and solving accordingly.

as your opponent folds more or less often against your all-in.
